A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCIP work. Their complete main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original MCIP Guardian training and evaluation results, including model comparisons in Table 2 and recall and training-progress analyses in Figures 6–7.

after.justification: v5 retains the original empirical results in Table 2 and Figures 6–7. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same MCI tracking-log representation, MCIP Guardian, taxonomy-guided data generation, and supervised fine-tuning procedure. Sections 3–6 introduce no changed method component.

E1.justification: Both use Glaive function-calling data, ToolACE generalization cases, and BFCL-v3 utility evaluation. The same ten risk categories and safe class are retained, with no added dataset, task, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same three xLAM-2 sizes, ToolACE-2-8B, two Qwen2.5-Instruct sizes, and DeepSeek-R1. The comparator subset in Figure 6 also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Benchmark construction, evaluation metrics, sample counts, and training settings match. Both report 2,218 benchmark instances, 13,830 training instances, and the same three-epoch training configuration; Table 5's evaluation prompt is unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7.2 retains the same recall-based overapproval analysis and training-progress analysis of the safety–utility trade-off. Figures 6–7 and Appendix A's illustrative cases provide no added or revised analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Both retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2's numerical results are unchanged, including Guardian's 65.79% BFCL accuracy, 54.16% Risk Resistance, 41.64% ToolACE Risk Resistance, and 75.73% Safety Awareness. Plotted results, qualitative findings, and appendix statistics also match.

T1.justification: The five-element information-flow definition, ordered trajectories, and taxonomy scope definitions in Sections 2.3–4 are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion preserve the same protocol, taxonomy, benchmark, and Guardian claims. The claimed safety and generalization improvements and first-evaluation positioning remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations concerning general reasoning, function-call overapproval, and the safety–utility trade-off. Limitations concerning attack coverage, absolute risk-identification performance, and scarce causal-dependency examples are unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds a first-page footnote identifying a public MCIP code repository, absent from v1. This adds code-access information; hardware, hyperparameters, data-generation details, and Appendix C's prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 expands existing citation lists with works including TopicAttack, Privacy Checklist, and Context Reasoner. These additions support the background in Sections 1, 2.3, and 4.2 without substantively changing comparisons with prior research or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v5 adjusts author-name capitalization, corrects an email address, identifies the corresponding author, changes 'Limitation' to 'Limitations', and adds acknowledgments. The core prose, section sequence, and appendix content remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables retain their content and design. Figure 5 moves from PDF page 7 to page 8, where Figures 5 and 6 are stacked in the left column; surrounding text and references reflow without added or removed displays.

improvement.justification: v5 provides an explicit MCIP code location missing from v1, improving implementation-access information, and adds supporting references for contextual integrity and attacks. These are limited improvements: the method, empirical evidence, analyses, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
